quests.sentence: The researcher reported that global temperatures had risen by 1.5 degrees over the decade.
quests.hint: 'Reported' is past tense - the reporting has already happened.
quests.explanation: 'Reported' is the simple past. The sentence describes a completed past act of reporting.

quests.sentence: The researcher reports that global temperatures continue to rise every single year.
quests.hint: 'Reports' is present tense - this is what is being said now.
quests.explanation: 'Reports' is the present simple, describing what the researcher is currently saying.

quests.sentence: The researcher predicts that temperatures will rise by a further two degrees by 2100.
quests.hint: 'Will rise by 2100' is a future prediction.
quests.explanation: 'Will rise' is the future simple in a reported prediction. 'By 2100' is a future time marker.

quests.sentence: If she had caught an earlier train, she would have arrived before the meeting began.
quests.hint: 'Would have arrived' is the past hypothetical result - she missed the earlier train.
quests.explanation: 'Would have arrived' is the past modal perfect in a third conditional. The earlier train was not caught.

quests.sentence: If she catches the early train, she always arrives with plenty of time to spare.
quests.hint: 'Always arrives' signals a current regular pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Catches' and 'arrives' are present simple forms in a zero conditional describing a current routine.

quests.sentence: If she catches the early train tomorrow, she will arrive before the meeting starts.
quests.hint: 'Tomorrow' is a future time, and 'will arrive' is the future result.
quests.explanation: 'Will arrive' is the future simple in a first conditional. 'Tomorrow' confirms this is a future scenario.

quests.sentence: The novel was translated into over thirty languages within a year of its first publication.
quests.hint: 'Was translated' is the past simple passive - the translation happened in the past.
quests.explanation: 'Was translated' is the past simple passive. 'Within a year of publication' is a completed past time frame.

quests.sentence: The novel is taught and studied at university literature departments around the world.
quests.hint: 'Is taught' is the present simple passive for an ongoing practice.
quests.explanation: 'Is taught' is the present simple passive, describing a current, ongoing academic practice.

quests.sentence: The novel will be adapted into a major film by a well-known Hollywood director.
quests.hint: 'Will be adapted' is the future simple passive - the film doesn't exist yet.
quests.explanation: 'Will be adapted' is the future simple passive. The film adaptation is a planned future project.

quests.sentence: She must have spent hours on the preparations - the house looked absolutely immaculate.
quests.hint: 'Must have spent' is a past deduction based on the evidence of how the house looked.
quests.explanation: 'Must have spent' is the past modal perfect used for a confident past deduction from evidence.

quests.sentence: She must spend a great deal of time maintaining her beautiful and well-kept garden.
quests.hint: 'Must spend' is a present deduction based on the visible state of the garden.
quests.explanation: 'Must spend' is a present modal used for logical deduction from present evidence.

quests.sentence: If she continues this level of preparation, she will certainly impress every guest.
quests.hint: 'Will certainly impress' is a confident future prediction.
quests.explanation: 'Will certainly impress' is the future simple. 'If she continues' is a future condition.

quests.sentence: Once the project had been fully completed, the tired team finally allowed itself to relax.
quests.hint: 'Once the project had been completed' is a past point - relaxing came after.
quests.explanation: 'Had been completed' is the past perfect passive. The completion preceded the relaxing, both in the past.

quests.sentence: Once the project is complete, the team always celebrates with a meal out together.
quests.hint: 'Always celebrates' signals a regular current pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Is complete' and 'celebrates' are present forms in a zero conditional, describing a current routine.

quests.sentence: Once the current project is finished, the team will take a well-deserved holiday.
quests.hint: 'Will take' is the future result after a future event.
quests.explanation: 'Will take' is the future simple in a first conditional. 'Once the project is finished' is a future condition.

quests.sentence: By the time the audit was complete, all the financial data had been thoroughly checked.
quests.hint: 'Had been checked' was done before the audit ended - both are past.
quests.explanation: 'Had been checked' is the past perfect passive. The checking was completed before another past event.

quests.sentence: All submitted data is currently being analysed by the independent research team.
quests.hint: 'Currently being analysed' signals an ongoing present action.
quests.explanation: 'Is being analysed' is the present continuous passive for an action in progress right now.

quests.sentence: All findings will have been reviewed and published before the conference begins.
quests.hint: 'Before the conference begins' is a future event - reviewing will be done first.
quests.explanation: 'Will have been reviewed' is the future perfect passive. The reviewing will be complete before a future event.

quests.sentence: After she had finished her double shift, she drove straight to the hospital.
quests.hint: 'After she had finished' is the earlier past event - the drive came after.
quests.explanation: 'Had finished' is the past perfect, showing the first in a sequence of past events.

quests.sentence: After she finishes her shift, she always goes straight home to have dinner with her family.
quests.hint: 'Always goes' signals a regular current habit.
quests.explanation: 'Finishes' and 'goes' are present simple forms in a zero conditional pattern.

quests.sentence: After she finishes her last shift of the year tomorrow, she will drive to the airport.
quests.hint: 'Tomorrow' is a future time - the shift will be finished, then she drives.
quests.explanation: 'Will drive' is the future simple. 'Tomorrow' and 'after she finishes' are future time references.

quests.sentence: The sudden decision to close the factory left thousands of local families in great difficulty.
quests.hint: 'Left' is past tense - this event has already happened.
quests.explanation: 'Left' is the simple past. No explicit marker is needed - the verb form tells us this is a completed past event.

quests.sentence: Decisions to close or relocate factories profoundly affect entire local communities.
quests.hint: This is a general truth - what is always the case.
quests.explanation: 'Affect' is the present simple expressing a general truth about the effect of factory closures.

quests.sentence: The planned expansion of the factory will create hundreds of well-paid local jobs.
quests.hint: 'Will create' is the future simple - this hasn't happened yet.
quests.explanation: 'Will create' is the future simple. 'Planned expansion' implies this is a future development.

quests.sentence: Although she had worked exceptionally hard, she narrowly missed out on the promotion.
quests.hint: 'Although she had worked' is a past concession - the effort and result are both past.
quests.explanation: 'Had worked' and 'missed' are past forms. 'Although' introduces a past concessive clause.

quests.sentence: Although she works very hard, she rarely receives the full recognition she truly deserves.
quests.hint: 'Works' and 'receives' are present forms - this is an ongoing situation.
quests.explanation: 'Works' and 'receives' are present simple forms. 'Although' introduces a present concessive clause.

quests.sentence: Although the final task will be very challenging, she will give it her absolute best effort.
quests.hint: 'Will be' and 'will give' are future forms - this hasn't happened yet.
quests.explanation: 'Will be' and 'will give' are future simple forms. 'Although' introduces a concessive clause about a future challenge.

quests.sentence: Had she been informed of the delay in time, she would have taken an earlier flight.
quests.hint: 'Had she been informed' is an inverted third conditional - past hypothetical.
quests.explanation: 'Had she been informed' is an inverted past perfect conditional. 'Would have taken' is the past hypothetical result.

quests.sentence: Were the company to change its pricing structure, many customers would leave immediately.
quests.hint: 'Were the company to change' is a formal present hypothetical.
quests.explanation: 'Were... to change' is a formal inverted conditional expressing a present hypothetical scenario.

quests.sentence: Should the right opportunity present itself, she will certainly take it without hesitation.
quests.hint: 'Should the opportunity present itself' is a future open condition.
quests.explanation: 'Should... present itself' is a formal inverted conditional. 'Will take' is the future result.
